chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Pops Foster's disastrous tuba
summary: The hall owner wanted a tuba player so Mutt rented one for Pops Foster, who played it so badly he was told to stick to bass fiddle.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Ory had left, and you went to work with Mutt, you were saying, in the Liberty Dance Hall.
Because I've got a whole tape I want to do with you about Ory.
And who was in that band at the time? Do you remember?
Well, they had Alex Hill on piano, Frank Passy(?)...
Oh, yeah, Frank Passley(?). Because we got some of them on yesterday's tape, but I wasn't sure.
Yeah, Frank Passley(?) was from New Orleans. Alex Hill, incidentally, wasn't from New Orleans. He was from a town called North Little Rock, Arkansas -- Argenna(?). Argenna, Arkansas.
Yeah. Well, and Pops Foster, Frownin'(?) George they called him. The guy wanted a tuba player, too.
That's exactly what ...(?)... was telling me.

And Mutt told him.... But this guy who owned this dance hall says, "Look, I don't care who he is. I don't care how good he plays that bass fiddle. I want a guy who plays tuba, too." And Papa Mutt naturally wanted George, for some reason, and he said, "Well, Pops Foster can play a tuba, too." So when George got to Los Angeles, he said, "Well, I can blow on one, a few notes." So Papa Mutt went and rented him one! And he played it so bad until the guy said, "Well, just let him play that bass fiddle and get rid of that bass horn" -- so they just took it back.
I've seen pictures of George Foster playing bass horn out here with somebody. Did he ever play bass horn that well?
No, he wasn't playing too good. Because I know after a week, the guy told Papa Mutt, "Tell him to forget it."
